correctness.rationale: For finite nonempty S and permutation alpha with theta(x)=x(alpha(x))^k also bijective, k>=2, F=theta circ alpha^{-1} permutes S and F(y)<=_L y^k<=_L y^2<=_L y. Around each finite F cycle principal left ideals cannot strictly decrease, so y L y^2; writing y=u y^2 implies y=u^{N-1}y^N for every N. Pick N>=2 with e=y^N idempotent; y=u^{N-1}e so ye=y, and y commutes with e hence ey=y. Since e commutes with y and y^N=e, y^{N-1} is the inverse of y in local monoid eSe. Thus S union of groups. Conversely for even k choose a positive a by CRT avoiding a=0 and 1+ka=0 modulo each prime of subgroup exponent E: at p=2 even k leaves 1 available; odd p leaves >=1 of p residues. Then x->x^a and x->x^{1+ka} permute all maximal subgroups and S. Odd-k C2 fails, and k=1 not asserted. Independent enumeration of all 122 labeled semigroup tables on 1,2,3 elements (1+8+113) found no disagreements for even k=2,4; general theorem is the principal-ideal and CRT argument.
